blockers.title: WorkflowTriggerType.SCHEDULED does not exist — AttributeError at runtime
blockers.description: The enum in common/common_semi/model/workflow.py defines SCHEDULE (not SCHEDULED). Every cron-triggered run will crash with AttributeError: 'SCHEDULED' is not a valid WorkflowTriggerType. Fix: change WorkflowTriggerType.SCHEDULED → WorkflowTriggerType.SCHEDULE on line 153.

blockers.title: Duplicate Alembic revision ID a1b2c3d4e5f6 — migrations will not run
blockers.description: Revision ID a1b2c3d4e5f6 is already claimed by the existing migration a1b2c3d4e5f6_grant_sequence_permissions.py. Alembic will abort with DuplicateRevisionError on the first deployment. Additionally, aa9b2ce1ed04_ingestion_changes.py has down_revision pointing at the existing file, creating an irreconcilable fork. Fix: generate a fresh unique 12-char hex revision ID and rename the file to match.

blockers.title: stdlib logging.getLogger used with structlog kwargs — TypeError kills FastAPI at startup
blockers.description: Python's stdlib Logger.info/warning/error only accept exc_info, stack_info, stacklevel, and extra as kwargs. The file uses structlog-style calls (e.g. logger.info('workflow_scheduler_started', loaded_schedules=len(schedules)) on line 70). This raises TypeError and propagates through the FastAPI lifespan, killing the process. Fix: replace logging.getLogger(__name__) with get_logger(component='backend.schedule_service') from common_semi.observe, matching every other backend module.

blockers.title: apscheduler>=3.10.0 unbounded — APScheduler 4.x removes AsyncIOScheduler and CronTrigger
blockers.description: APScheduler 4.x is a complete rewrite that removed apscheduler.schedulers.asyncio and apscheduler.triggers.cron. The constraint >=3.10.0 has no upper bound; any future uv lock --upgrade or fresh CI resolution could pull 4.x and cause ImportError at service startup. The uv.lock currently pins 3.11.3 (safe) but the pyproject.toml must be fixed. Fix: change to apscheduler>=3.10.0,<4.0.

blockers.title: update_schedule stores raw datetime in updates dict — JSON serialization error
blockers.description: updates['next_run_at'] = _compute_next_run(cron, tz) assigns a timezone-aware datetime object. All other DB-bound date values in the codebase (e.g. _trigger_scheduled_run lines 174-175) explicitly call .isoformat() before passing to the repository. The Supabase/postgrest-py client JSON-serializes the updates dict and will raise TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable. Fix: updates['next_run_at'] = next_run.isoformat() if next_run else None.

blockers.title: Missing _validate_storage_url_org_scope allows cross-org file access via schedule parameters
blockers.description: Both create_workflow_schedule and update_workflow_schedule accept a parameters dict that is stored and passed directly to create_workflow_run when the cron fires. Manual run paths (lines 457, 1129) call _validate_storage_url_org_scope to prevent cross-org storage URL access, but the schedule endpoints skip this check. An attacker can store a minio://bucket/workflow-inputs/OTHER_ORG_UUID/... path in schedule parameters and trigger read access to another org's uploaded files on every cron fire. Fix: call await _validate_storage_url_org_scope(db, body.parameters, user_id) in both create and update handlers before persisting.

blockers.title: No tests for any new schedule endpoints or schedule service
blockers.description: backend.md convention requires at minimum: a happy-path integration test via TestClient, a unit test for the core service logic, and an error-case test (404, 422). Zero test files reference WorkflowSchedule, schedule_service, or the /schedules endpoints. Critical paths with no coverage include: cron validation errors, org authorization checks, scheduler startup/shutdown, and the _trigger_scheduled_run execution path.

suggestions.title: Disabled schedule not removed from APScheduler when detected in _trigger_scheduled_run
suggestions.description: When _trigger_scheduled_run detects is_enabled=False it returns early without calling self._remove_job(schedule_id). The APScheduler job continues firing on every cron interval causing perpetual DB round-trips. Fix: call self._remove_job(schedule_id) before the early return.

suggestions.title: _validate_cron double-wraps its own ValueError message
suggestions.description: When croniter.is_valid() returns False, line 254 raises ValueError('Invalid cron expression: ...') which is immediately caught by except Exception and re-raised as ValueError(f"Invalid cron expression: ... — Invalid cron expression: ..."). The 422 detail users receive has the message duplicated. Fix: move the if not is_valid: raise outside the try/except so only exceptions thrown by croniter.is_valid() itself are caught.

suggestions.title: Invalid IANA timezone accepted — schedule silently never fires
suggestions.description: Cron expressions are validated via _validate_cron, but timezone strings are not validated. An invalid timezone (e.g. 'NotReal/Zone') is persisted and returns HTTP 201. Both _compute_next_run and _register_job silently swallow ZoneInfo errors, so no APScheduler job is ever registered. The schedule appears created but never fires. Fix: validate timezone with zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(timezone) in a try/except in create_schedule and update_schedule, raising ValueError on failure.

suggestions.title: list_workflow_schedules and create_workflow_schedule use orgs[0] inconsistently
suggestions.description: list_workflow_schedules and create_workflow_schedule use orgs[0].id (first org only), while get, update, and delete correctly build org_ids = {str(o.id) for o in orgs} and check membership. For multi-org users, list only shows one org's schedules and create forces the schedule into that org regardless of which org the referenced workflow_type belongs to.

suggestions.title: list_all_enabled silently truncates at PostgREST default limit of 1000
suggestions.description: The startup query has no .limit() or pagination. Supabase/PostgREST caps results at 1000 rows by default. With more than 1000 enabled schedules, the excess silently never fire after restart with no log warning or error. Fix: add .limit(10000) (or paginate) and log a warning if len(schedules) == limit.

suggestions.title: 12-field WorkflowScheduleResponse construction copy-pasted across 5 handlers
suggestions.description: The WorkflowScheduleResponse(...) block with 12 fields is duplicated identically in all five schedule handlers. Any new field on WorkflowSchedule must be added in five separate places. Fix: add a @classmethod from_schedule(cls, schedule, workflow_type: str) to WorkflowScheduleResponse.

suggestions.title: Redundant definition lookup per trigger — definition fetched twice
suggestions.description: _trigger_scheduled_run fetches the workflow type definition to get prefect_deployment_name, then create_workflow_run fetches the same definition again by name. Consider passing prefect_deployment_name directly or storing it as a denormalized column on workflow_schedules.

blockers.title: Schedule endpoints crash with AttributeError when org objects are dicts
blockers.description: All 5 new schedule endpoints access orgs[0].id directly. Existing endpoints throughout this file use an isinstance(o, dict) guard (confirmed at lines 149, 348, 379) because user_repository.get_organizations() can return raw dicts. When that code path is hit, every schedule endpoint raises AttributeError and returns a 500. Fix: use the established project pattern, e.g. str(orgs[0].get('id') if isinstance(orgs[0], dict) else orgs[0].id).

blockers.title: _validate_cron double-wraps ValueError, corrupting error messages
blockers.description: When croniter.is_valid() returns False, the code raises ValueError inside the try block. That ValueError is immediately caught by except Exception as exc, and a second ValueError is raised with str(exc) embedded — producing 'Invalid cron expression: "expr" — Invalid cron expression: "expr"'. The intent was to catch exceptions thrown *by* is_valid, not the manually-raised one. Fix: check the result separately before entering the try, or narrow the except to non-ValueError exceptions.

blockers.title: No tests for any of the 5 new schedule endpoints
blockers.description: Five new endpoints (list, create, get, update, delete) and the _trigger_scheduled_run scheduling logic have zero unit or integration tests. The conftest only mocks out the scheduler to prevent startup side-effects — no test exercises any schedule endpoint path. Project convention (global-review.md) requires new API endpoints to have corresponding tests.

blockers.title: Scheduler conftest mock patches wrong module binding
blockers.description: The autouse fixture patches 'core.sse.listeners.workflow_scheduler', but the workflow router binds the singleton independently via 'from modules.v2.workflow.schedule_service import workflow_scheduler' (workflow.py line 43). The two bindings are independent: the patch only affects the listeners module, leaving the router's reference pointing to the real, unstarted AsyncIOScheduler. Any test that calls a schedule endpoint will hit _register_job or _remove_job on the live scheduler and raise RuntimeError: The scheduler has not been started yet. Fix: also patch 'modules.v2.workflow.schedule_service.workflow_scheduler' or the router's binding directly.

suggestions.title: last_run_at is updated even when the scheduled trigger fails
suggestions.description: The DB update block is outside the try/except, so last_run_at is stamped as 'now' regardless of whether create_workflow_run succeeded. Systematic failures (Prefect unreachable, etc.) become invisible — the schedule appears healthy in the UI and monitoring queries.

suggestions.title: Invalid IANA timezone silently creates a non-functional schedule
suggestions.description: _validate_cron validates only the cron expression. A bad timezone string causes CronTrigger.from_crontab to raise inside _register_job, which is caught and swallowed. The DB row is inserted and HTTP 201 is returned, but the job is never registered — the schedule fires no runs silently. Fix: add timezone validation that raises ValueError for unknown IANA keys before the DB insert.

suggestions.title: tzdata package missing — next_run_at will always be NULL in prod Docker
suggestions.description: The production image uses python:3.12-slim, which strips /usr/share/zoneinfo. zoneinfo.ZoneInfo() raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError on slim. _compute_next_run() silently catches this and returns None, so next_run_at is never written. APScheduler uses its own bundled pytz so scheduling still fires, but the UI next-run display is permanently blank. Fix: add 'tzdata>=2024.1' to pyproject.toml.

suggestions.title: Sync Supabase .execute() blocks the asyncio event loop inside APScheduler
suggestions.description: The supabase.Client is synchronous — each .execute() call is a blocking HTTP request with no await. AsyncIOScheduler dispatches async jobs directly on the uvicorn event loop via ensure_future(). The three blocking calls in _trigger_scheduled_run (~30-90 ms total per trigger) stall the event loop during that time, starving all other requests and APScheduler tick precision. Fix: wrap each blocking repository call in asyncio.to_thread().

suggestions.title: Stored parameters not re-validated at trigger time (storage URL org scoping)
suggestions.description: _validate_storage_url_org_scope is enforced at create and update time but not when the scheduler fires. If a user is removed from an org after schedule creation, or if parameters are modified via a direct DB write, the trigger will execute with potentially cross-org file references. Fix: call _validate_storage_url_org_scope inside _trigger_scheduled_run before invoking create_workflow_run.

suggestions.title: Multi-org users can only list/create schedules for their first org
suggestions.description: list_workflow_schedules and create_workflow_schedule use orgs[0] as the org scope. The get/update/delete endpoints correctly build a set of all org IDs. A multi-org user cannot list or create schedules for any non-primary org.

suggestions.title: 404 vs 403 response reveals schedule existence across org boundaries
suggestions.description: GET/PATCH/DELETE return 404 if the schedule doesn't exist and 403 if it belongs to another org. An attacker can distinguish the two cases to confirm whether a UUID is a valid schedule ID in another org. Practical risk is low (UUID v4 search space), but violates tenant isolation principles. Fix: return 404 in both cases, or filter by both id and org_id in the DB query.

suggestions.title: APScheduler is started before enabled schedules are loaded from the database
suggestions.description: start() calls self._scheduler.start() then fetches schedules from DB. During the await for the DB fetch, the scheduler is running but has no jobs registered. A cron that fires in this narrow window is missed (recovered by misfire_grace_time=300s). The idiomatic APScheduler pattern is: fetch schedules → register all jobs → start scheduler.

suggestions.title: Org-lookup boilerplate copy-pasted across 5 endpoints with inconsistent empty-org handling
suggestions.description: The user_id/orgs/org_id block is repeated in all 5 endpoints with a subtle inconsistency: list/create raise 403 'User has no organisation' when orgs is empty, but get/update/delete fall through to a 403 'Not authorised to X this schedule'. Should be extracted to a shared FastAPI dependency.

suggestions.title: croniter has no upper version bound
suggestions.description: croniter>=2.0.0 without an upper cap allows any future 3.x. croniter 2.x→3.x has included breaking API changes historically. Consider pinning to <3.0 to match the apscheduler<4.0 pattern already used.

suggestions.title: DB generator obtained for scheduler is never closed
suggestions.description: __anext__() advances the generator but aclose() is never called. The comment notes today's get_supabase_database has no teardown, so it's harmless now — but any future cleanup added after its yield will silently not run for the scheduler session. Produces ResourceWarning under strict GC modes.

blockers.title: Excursion search path: tuple assigned to items instead of list
blockers.description: In the `if query:` branch, `items = await excursion_service.list_excursions(...)` assigns the full 2-tuple `(list_of_dicts, total_count)` returned by `list_excursions` to `items`, because `filters` contains `search=query`. This tuple is then emitted as `"items": items` in the response. Every search request on the excursions endpoint returns `[[{...excursion dicts...}], count]` instead of `[{...excursion dicts...}]`, breaking all clients. The `else` branch correctly handles this with `items = items_and_count[0] if isinstance(items_and_count, tuple) else items_and_count`, but that guard was not applied in the new `if query:` path. Fix: unpack the tuple — `items, _ = await excursion_service.list_excursions(...)` or use `items_and_count[0]`.

blockers.title: Invalid timezone silently creates a permanently dead schedule
blockers.description: create_schedule validates the cron expression via _validate_cron but does not validate the timezone string. If an invalid IANA timezone is supplied: (1) _compute_next_run catches ZoneInfoNotFoundError silently and returns None; (2) the schedule is persisted to the DB with is_enabled=True but next_run_at=None; (3) _register_job calls CronTrigger.from_crontab with the bad timezone which raises, logs a warning, and returns — no APScheduler job is ever registered. The API returns 201 Created with no error, but the schedule never fires. The same path exists in update_schedule when timezone is in updates. On every subsequent restart the startup loader hits the same failure for this row and again registers no job. Fix: add _validate_timezone(tz_name) that raises ValueError on ZoneInfoNotFoundError, and call it from both create_schedule and update_schedule (the route handler already converts ValueError to HTTP 422).

suggestions.title: No rate limit or per-org schedule cap on POST /{workflow_type}/schedules
suggestions.description: create_workflow_schedule has no rate limiting and no cap on how many schedules an org can create. A user could create N schedules with cron_expression='* * * * *' (valid, fires every minute) via repeated POST calls. APScheduler fires all N _trigger_scheduled_run coroutines per minute, each making Supabase reads and a Prefect submission. The existing check_rate_limit helper (used by presigned-URL upload and catalog endpoints) is not applied here. Consider adding a per-user rate limit and a per-org schedule count cap before insert.

suggestions.title: extra_workflow_run_ids passed to list_excursions is silently ignored
suggestions.description: resolve_search_workflow_run_ids resolves run IDs via product/BU/foundry search and passes them as extra_workflow_run_ids in the filters dict to list_excursions. However, inside list_excursions the search branch (_collect_matching_excursion_ids) does not read this key — it performs its own product lookup internally. The extra_run_ids computation is wasted work and the intended per-product run-ID narrowing has no effect on search results.

suggestions.title: policy_repository.py not registered in __init__ or AppDatabase
suggestions.description: PolicyRepository and PolicyVersionRepository are defined in this new file but not exported from db/repositories/__init__.py, not added to __all__, and not wired into AppDatabase. If any service code tries to use db.policy_repository it will fail with AttributeError. If these stubs are intentionally orphaned for now, the file should include a comment indicating its status.
